name: The Keller Twelve
notes: Beginner hypertrophy block for a 167 cm / 50 kg lifter training alone five evenings a week in a basement gym, on a 60-minute session ceiling. Every load in this file is snapped to the plate lattice described in inventory.json -- change the inventory and regenerate with tools/gen.py rather than editing loads by hand. Cardio is deliberately capped so it does not eat the caloric surplus.

nutritionPhases.note: Start here. ~52 kcal/kg -- two liquid meals a day make this easy.
TDEE has risen with your bodyweight. So does the target.
Final push. If the waist is growing faster than the lifts, cut 200.

rules: Eat in surplus every single day. A missed meal is a missed session.
Leave 2 reps in the tank -- 3 to 4 during weeks 1 to 4.
Collars on. Check them mid-set. Spinlock collars work loose under load.
Never fail alone under a bar. Set the catch pins, or press dumbbells.
Add weight only when you earn it: top of the rep range on every set.
Log every set. A session you didn't log is a session you can't beat next week.
Sixty minutes means sixty minutes. If you are over, cut the last superset -- not the main lift, not the warm-up.
If something hurts -- not burns, HURTS -- stop the set, log the niggle, use the substitute.

cardioProgression.note: Calves and Achilles need four weeks to adapt. Don't rush this.
The bag appears. Wraps or gloves, always.

strengthTargets.note: e1RM ~42 kg, 0.76x bodyweight. A FLOOR, not a goal.
e1RM ~23 kg. The slowest-moving lift you own -- that is normal.
3 to 6 strict reps by week 12. The most satisfying number here.

blocks.name: Foundation
blocks.summary: Full body three times a week. Light loads, perfect reps, every barbell lift introduced with the empty bar. Build the eating habit here.

days.title: Full Body A
days.note: Squat-led. Every load is deliberately light — you are rehearsing patterns, not testing yourself. The four weeks you spend here are the four you don't lose to a tweaked back in week six.

warnings.title: Set the catch pins
warnings.body: Before your first work set, set the stand's catch pins just below your bottom position. Miss a rep and you sit down; the bar lands on steel.

warnings.title: Collars on, checked mid-set
warnings.body: Spinlock collars work loose under load. A plate sliding off one end is the single most likely injury in your room.

drills.note: On the interlocking mats, never bare concrete.
Wide grip, over the head and behind.

prescriptions.coachNote: EMPTY BAR in week 1. No exceptions. Brace as if someone is about to punch your stomach, then sit down and stand up.
Same bar, add plates. The bar stays in contact with your legs the whole way down. If it drifts forward, your lower back takes it.
Bodyweight on purpose, so the one dumbbell stays loaded through the whole superset. If you can't get 8, put your hands on the bench and do them at an incline.
Pull to the hip pocket, not the armpit. One full second at the top.
The second your lower back sags, the set is over. Reset rather than holding a bad shape.

days.title: Skip, Run & Core
days.note: Easy means easy. This session exists for your heart and your calves, not to burn calories — you need those.

prescriptions.coachNote: Skipping wrecks untrained calves and Achilles tendons, so we ramp it over four weeks.
Conversational pace. If you cannot speak a full sentence, you are going too fast.
Three-round circuit with the side plank and hollow hold.

days.title: Full Body B
days.note: Hinge-led, and the day that teaches you the deadlift and the overhead press — the two lifts a beginner is most often thrown into cold.

warnings.title: Bar height — read before your first pull
warnings.body: Your plates are small-diameter, so a lightly loaded bar sits too low and forces your back to round at the start. Stack the two 20 kg tri-grips flat and rest each end of the bar on them until your working weight has enough plates to raise it naturally — around 50 kg with the 20s on.

warnings.title: Check the ceiling
warnings.body: Measure your overhead clearance before pressing. The basement beams and pipes are not at a uniform height.

warnings.title: Collars on, checked mid-set
warnings.body: Spinlock collars work loose under load. A plate sliding off one end is the single most likely injury in your room.

prescriptions.coachNote: EMPTY BAR from the blocks in week 1. Take the slack out of the bar before you pull — you should hear it click. Set it down and reset every rep.
Empty bar in week 1. Ribs down, glutes and abs locked. Leaning back to move the weight means it is too heavy.
The more horizontal your body, the harder it gets. Log your foot position so you can repeat it.
Depth is whatever you can hold without the lower back rounding. That point is your depth for now.
Lower back pressed flat into the mat the entire time.

days.title: Rest
days.note: A real rest day. Eat your full target, get eight hours, walk if you feel like moving. Muscle is built on the days you don't train — the session only sends the signal.

days.title: Full Body C
days.note: Press-led, plus the first work towards a pull-up. You will not get a pull-up by trying pull-ups — you get it by lowering yourself slowly, over and over.

warnings.title: Bench pins at chest height
warnings.body: Set the pins so a failed rep lands on them and not on you. Never take the bench press to failure alone.

warnings.title: Collars on, checked mid-set
warnings.body: Spinlock collars work loose under load. A plate sliding off one end is the single most likely injury in your room.

prescriptions.coachNote: Empty bar in week 1. Feet flat, shoulder blades pinched back and down, bar to the lower chest, elbows at 45-60 degrees.
Same bar as the bench. Pull to the navel. If your torso rises with every rep, the weight is winning.
Step or jump to the top, then fight the way down for a full five seconds. This is the fastest route to your first strict pull-up.
Bodyweight only for four weeks. Brutal for a bodyweight movement — that is normal, don't add load.
Partial range. If your back arches at all, swap for a 3 x 40 s plank until week 3.

days.title: Rest
days.note: Off. Cook something big — Saturday is the easiest day of the week to bank a 3,000 kcal day, and a good week of eating covers a mediocre week of training.

prescriptions.coachNote: The longer of your two runs. Same conversational pace.
From the rings or the wall bar. Relax into it — this decompresses everything the squats and rows compressed all week.

blocks.name: Build
blocks.summary: Upper/Lower across four days. Every movement pattern gets two exposures a week, every upper day presses and pulls, and the accessories are supersetted so it all fits in 60 minutes.

days.title: Lower A · Squat
days.note: Quads, glutes and the whole brace. If you only ever do one thing properly, make it this squat.

warnings.title: Set the catch pins
warnings.body: Before your first work set, set the stand's catch pins just below your bottom position. Miss a rep and you sit down; the bar lands on steel.

warnings.title: Collars on, checked mid-set
warnings.body: Spinlock collars work loose under load. A plate sliding off one end is the single most likely injury in your room.

prescriptions.coachNote: The most important set of your week. Drive the whole foot through the floor coming up — don't let the hips shoot up first.
Same bar, strip to the RDL weight once. Squeeze the glutes to stand up rather than pulling with the lower back.
Torso slightly forward loads the glute, upright loads the quad. Pick one and stay consistent.
On the edge of the step platform. Bodyweight on purpose — no plate change inside the superset. Full stretch at the bottom, 2-second squeeze at the top.
No swinging. Curl the pelvis up towards the ribs, don't just lift the thighs.
You are already hanging on the bar, so this costs you almost nothing. A second vertical-pull exposure in the week is what buys you your first strict pull-up.

days.title: Upper A · Bench-led
days.note: 10 pressing sets and 10 pulling sets. Every upper day in this programme is balanced — that is the whole point of the rewrite.

warnings.title: Bench pins at chest height
warnings.body: Set the pins so a failed rep lands on them and not on you. Never take the bench press to failure alone.

warnings.title: Collars on, checked mid-set
warnings.body: Spinlock collars work loose under load. A plate sliding off one end is the single most likely injury in your room.

prescriptions.coachNote: Bar to the lower chest, elbows at 45-60 degrees, drive up and slightly towards your face. Pins at chest height.
Same bar as the bench. This is the row v1 left out of push day — your shoulders need it on the same day you press.
Bench at its lower incline notch, roughly 30 degrees.
Use the wall cable — no plate change inside the superset. Elbows high and wide, rotating the hands back. The insurance policy on every press you do.
Elbows pinned to the ribs. Lower over 3 seconds — the negative is where the arm grows.
Bare handles, or the fixed vinyl dumbbells. Lead with the elbows. There is no such thing as a heavy lateral raise.

days.title: Easy Run or Nothing
days.note: Genuinely optional. Take it if you slept well and ate enough; skip it without guilt if you are sore, behind on food, or the week is heavy. At your bodyweight, extra cardio is a cost, not a bonus.

prescriptions.coachNote: Zone 2. If you cannot breathe through your nose, you are going too fast.

days.title: Lower B · Deadlift
days.note: Deadlift day. The heaviest thing you lift all week and the lift with the least margin for sloppy technique. Five reps, never more, never to failure.

warnings.title: Bar height — read before your first pull
warnings.body: Your plates are small-diameter, so a lightly loaded bar sits too low and forces your back to round at the start. Stack the two 20 kg tri-grips flat and rest each end of the bar on them until your working weight has enough plates to raise it naturally — around 50 kg with the 20s on.

warnings.title: Pad the hip thrust bar
warnings.body: Fold the green mat over the bar. A bare bar on the hip bones ends the set early.

warnings.title: Collars on, checked mid-set
warnings.body: Spinlock collars work loose under load. A plate sliding off one end is the single most likely injury in your room.

prescriptions.coachNote: Three sets, not four — this is the highest-fatigue lift you own. Set it down and reset every rep. Never to failure.
Your second squat exposure of the week, and the one v1 was missing. Elbows high, torso vertical. Swap to a goblet squat if the wrists complain.
Squeeze hard at the top for a full second. Ribs stay down — don't arch the lower back to get higher.
Higher reps than Monday, same quality. No bouncing.
Walk the length of the basement without leaning away from it. Check the collars before you pick it up.
FROM WEEK 9 ONLY — skip this in weeks 5-8. Hook your feet under the squat stand. Lower as slowly as you can control; expect to fall fast at first.

days.title: Upper B · Press-led
days.note: 10 pressing sets and 10 pulling sets again. Back and biceps are what make a physique read as trained, and they are what beginners skimp on.

warnings.title: Check the ceiling
warnings.body: Measure your overhead clearance before pressing. The basement beams and pipes are not at a uniform height.

warnings.title: Collars on, checked mid-set
warnings.body: Spinlock collars work loose under load. A plate sliding off one end is the single most likely injury in your room.

prescriptions.coachNote: Glutes and abs locked. Head moves back, then through, as the bar passes. Leaning back to move it means it is too heavy.
Always stop one rep before failure. When you get 8 assisted, move to a thinner band. Log the band colour in the set note.
Bodyweight, so the dumbbells stay loaded through the whole superset. Walk your feet forward to make it harder.
Neutral grip, thumbs up. Hits the brachialis, which pushes the arm wider.
Wall cable — no plate change inside the superset. Elbows pinned to the ribs.

days.title: Rest
days.note: Complete rest after four lifting days. Cook, sleep in, meal-prep for the week. If you are twitchy, a 30-minute walk is all you get.

prescriptions.coachNote: Your one dedicated cardio session, 48 hours clear of Thursday's deadlifts and a full day before Monday's squat. Follow the cardio table.
Fast intervals. Balls of the feet, elbows in, wrists doing the work.
Wraps or gloves on, always. Straight punches, move your feet, breathe out on every shot. This lives on Sunday, not on lifting days — that is where v1's 77-minute sessions came from.

blocks.name: Deload
blocks.summary: Same four days, 70% of the load, 60% of the sets, supersets unwound so nothing is rushed. Bar speed stays fast. You will want to skip this week -- it is the week the previous three turn into muscle.

blocks.name: Push
blocks.summary: Same split, one set added to the lead lift of each day, 1 rep in reserve on those sets. Nordic curl negatives become non-optional on Thursday.

blocks.name: Test
blocks.summary: Five-rep tests on the four barbell lifts, max strict pull-ups, and the 5K. These five numbers seed cycle 2.

days.title: Test · Squat
days.note: Test week. Nothing to prove except what twelve weeks bought you.

days.note: Last lifting session of the cycle. Take the week-12 photos afterwards, while you are still pumped — same four poses, same spot, same light.
